newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kazakh man arrested in Seoul for drug trafficking.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh man arrested in Seoul for drug trafficking.

text.p: Police have detained a Kazakh man for attempting to smuggle heroin worth an estimated $4.8 million out of South Korea, police officers said on Friday.
Viktor Kim, 50, was stopped at Seoul's airport on Thursday when he carried one kg (2.2 lb) of heroin packed in a plastic bag inside his belt, an officer at the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said.
It is the largest volume among reported narcotic smuggling cases in South Korea, police said.
The police officer quoted Kim, an ethnic Korean, as saying that he had brought the heroin into the country on November 20 through the same airport without being detected by inspectors.
Kim told police he wanted to sell the heroin in South Korea but was unable to find buyers during his visit, he added.
South Korean laws call for the maximum penalty of death for narcotic trafficking.
